claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a reported hierarchical heterostructure featuring multilevel chemical fluctuations and phase heterogeneity.

Combining high-throughput microstructural characterization with a physics-informed data-driven surrogate will enable rapid and accurate prediction of Young’s modulus, yield strength, and toughness in HfNbTiVAl10.
The proposed hybrid approach will overcome the computational demands of full first-principles or phase-field simulations.
Existing approaches cannot reliably predict fracture properties in this material.
The proposed framework will extract descriptors of hierarchical chemical fluctuations and phase features from high-throughput microstructural images.
The regression model will incorporate constraints derived from CALPHAD and first-principles datasets.
Hierarchical chemical fluctuations determine local stress distributions in HfNbTiVAl10.
Phase heterogeneity determines crack-propagation paths in HfNbTiVAl10.
The extracted microstructural descriptors can capture the local stress and crack-path effects of the hierarchical heterostructure.
Detailed microstructural features can parameterize the local mechanical environment for the surrogate model.
Embedding CALPHAD and first-principles constraints will keep predictions of elastic response, plastic response, crack initiation, and crack propagation physically realistic.
The layered surrogate representation will reduce reliance on full-scale simulations without sacrificing predictive accuracy.
The proposed method will reduce computational time by approximately 10- to 20-fold relative to conventional full-scale simulations.
The proposed method will improve prediction accuracy by approximately 10% for Young’s modulus, yield strength, and fracture toughness relative to conventional full-scale simulations.
Existing first-principles, CALPHAD, and multi-step machine-learning approaches are computationally intensive.
Existing approaches typically lack robust predictions of toughness and fracture behavior.
The model may become unreliable when phase transformations or defect structures fall substantially outside the training distribution.
The model may become unreliable when its descriptors fail to capture nanoscale crack-initiation mechanisms.
A blinded prospective benchmark will compare model predictions against independently measured tensile and fracture properties for HfNbTiVAl10 samples with varied hierarchical microstructures.
The hypothesis is to be falsified if mean prediction discrepancy exceeds 10% or computational time is not reduced by at least tenfold.
